draft.status: Draft from a Mac that is not the reference Mac; not record.json, and no decision. The acceptance tests count every budget here as INCONCLUSIVE, which would force a native verdict this evidence does not support.
gaps: Budgets must be rerun on the reference Mac (Mac15,7, M3 Pro, 36 GB, mains, thermal nominal), then the decision written.

The five preflightMs runs predate windoliver/deepbuild#594, when perf rebuilt the Rust tree cold in temp copies. With that fix applied here, two preflights took 114 s and 108 s, with every perf comparison passing; the five runs are to be taken again.

Perf flagged repo-rules p50 (+50%) because the merge-base copy had no origin/main, so repo-rules skipped its size check there; #594's fix gives the copy one, and repo-rules then reads 265 ms against the base's 257 ms.
findings: Both agents wrote their panels from gpui-shell's docs and the brief alone, with no generated type declarations: Codex passed on round 0, Claude Code after one fix.
Claude Code's chart is a row of dots, not a line chart; the headless test checks texts and clicks, not the chart's form.
gpui-shell writes gpui-kit.d.ts and jsconfig.json into a panel's directory each time it loads it.
gpui-shell's release builds JIT hot functions to native code with no switch; debug builds, so the tests, stay on the interpreter.

Codex's panel keeps one alert on screen: a later symbol's crossing replaces an earlier one, where the brief says each alert stays shown. The headless test arms one symbol, so it passes; a test that arms two would catch it.

A binary's first launch after it is built or copied took 0.85-1.01 s here, against 150-310 ms after: macOS checks a new binary once. That is at or just over the 1 s budget, off the reference Mac; the budget runs follow one untimed launch.

menuBar.reason: gpui-kit has no menu-bar item, so the count is an AppKit NSStatusItem the app creates; GPUI's offscreen renderer captures only GPUI windows.
checks: menu_bar_title(sessions()), the title main.rs gives the status item, is 143
the window's count text, read back from its accessibility label, is the same 143
no test reads the NSStatusItem itself back: it is AppKit, not a GPUI element

rounds.fix: Round 0 stopped at Tick 99: its chart was a column of dots that grew a row per tick and pushed the next button below the 640 px window. Given the test's failure output, Claude Code laid the dots out horizontally.

deviation.reason: gpui-shell at M0 has no out-of-process panel host, and its release builds tier hot functions up to native code with no switch (shell_jit_config); debug builds, so the headless tests, stay on the interpreter. The spike loads the panel in the app through gpui-shell, as its Scope says. The heap, stack, microtask and pending limits and the 4 ms budget are the Fields' values, not enforced by this spike.
